proposal.name: Collect Go runtime evidence through the shared lifecycle

issue_plan.name: Collect Go runtime evidence through the shared lifecycle
issue_plan.summary: Two ordered plumbing changes add a production Go collector with a trusted framework channel and real local-process tests, then complete its base/candidate, deadline and queue integration. Together they cover the local runtime work in #536 and preserve existing discovery, fake-adapter and legacy contracts. Both changes keep current-state documentation accurate; configured factory admission stays closed and prepared-Docker transport remains the already ordered next step of #534. The merger records the new runtime decision using the existing selection/discovery decision D-0321 as a foundation.

issues.title: Collect authentic Go test outcomes through a reusable host transport
issues.body:
This is step 1 of 2 completing #536, the local runtime-collection step of #534 within #523/#513/#452. The base already has GoRepositoryAcceptanceAdapter.Select and Discover and the shared configured acceptance lifecycle. Add the reusable production Go runtime collector and a distinct local process transport fixture that calls production selection, discovery and collection through RepositoryAcceptanceEnvironment.RunAcceptance. This pull request establishes the collector's real framework outcomes and transport boundary; the next ordered issue exercises and completes the shared base/candidate, allowance and queue integration. The prepared-Docker runtime transport remains the separate second step of #534.

Implement the framework producer, lifecycle validation and conversion to RepositoryAcceptanceEvidence in production Go code under internal/plumbing, callable through a trusted host-owned transport boundary. A later Docker implementation must invoke this identical producer and collector unchanged. Keep transport operations, context propagation, partial-start resource ownership and cleanup explicit. Reuse go_acceptance.go and go_discovery.go; do not invent another selector or declaration-discovery policy. A local test fixture can own process launch and private temporary storage, but cannot implement the reporter, infer outcomes, manufacture JSON evidence or replace the production collector. Do not extend the existing discovery-only fixtures to execute tests.

Run each selector separately from its captured owning part's directory with the safely narrowed test_one argument array, following real package loading, verbatim-source and declaration checks and compilation. Preserve production sources, local dependencies, build constraints, ordinary and external test packages and local module ownership. Pin the complete (part, framework, file, selector) identity, verbatim acceptance bytes, discovered Go import path, source digest and captured execution digest throughout. Discovery of a parent declaration does not establish that a selected subtest exists.

Preserve the full grammar in docs/factory.md: direct literal go test; exactly one -run placeholder, separate or equal form, containing {test} or ^{test}$; omitted scope or one clean inclusive ., ./dir, ./... or ./dir/... scope. Preserve the existing refusal of widening, Go-skipped recursive directories and cross-module selection. Each slash-separated selector component is independently regexp-escaped and anchored; shell-looking text stays an argument. Preserve all supported flag semantics and argument boundaries: -tags, nonnegative -timeout including 0, one positive -parallel/-p/-cpu value, -shuffle off/on or integer seed, -mod readonly/vendor, -count exactly 1 with absent count added, and bare or =true/=false -short/-v/-race/-trimpath. Both value spellings remain supported. Do not silently omit or override flags to accommodate instrumentation. Unsupported, repeated or conflicting flags, wrappers, opaque commands, file/import-path/multiple scopes and other forms remain refused by Select before preparation or execution.

Collect authentic Go testing start and terminal events through a trusted channel independent of BOTH workload stdout and stderr. Any helper or framework hook comes from host-owned production code, uses only the pinned Go toolchain and standard library offline, and preserves acceptance source bytes and Go testing semantics, including TestMain, nested and parallel tests, skips and panic handling. Helper preparation cannot require Python, installation, downloads, network or host caches. Parsing go test output, test2json output or framing-looking diagnostic bytes into a new record format is not independent evidence. A process exit, successful compilation, synthetic exit failure or fabricated runner marker cannot establish test completion.

Retain sufficient authentic parent/child lifecycle to require exactly one requested selection, one authentic start and one terminal result. An ancestor, prefix, sibling, different parameter case or parameterized family cannot stand in for an exact requested child. Bind every converted record to the host's fresh InvocationID, complete identity, discovered import path, SourceDigest and ExecutionDigest before returning it through the shared evidence boundary. Reject duplicate, stale, contradictory, reordered, truncated, missing and mismatched lifecycle or bindings; do not attribute another file, package, module or part. Go-specific start requirements belong to this runtime path and must not become mandatory for the existing trusted fake adapters or for Run/ReadFile/Close-only environments.

An authentic completed assertion failure or panic with framework failure completion yields kind test/status failed. An authentic selected skip yields test/skipped and qualifies neither as a candidate pass nor as a base failure. Real pass, failure and skip records retain explanations. Zero-test success, an absent selector or child, TestMain exiting before m.Run, nonzero abrupt exit, interruption and missing terminal events do not establish completion. Preserve running, refused and not_run outcomes with reasons. Treat tool/helper preparation, package/discovery and compilation errors as setup/refusal outcomes, including compilation against a proposed API. Precise compiler attribution remains outside #534 in the already ordered later issue of #523; preserve the fake adapters' existing attributable compile-failure contract.

Add default Go acceptance and regression coverage with small standard-library-only temporary modules and isolated temporary caches, using actual Go loading, compilation and execution plus the production collector. No Docker, network, opt-in or substituted JSON producer is permitted for framework-outcome tests. Demonstrate one unchanged acceptance source failing a real assertion against base production code and passing after changing only a production file. Check top-level and exact nested selectors, parallel children, regexp punctuation and shell-looking names, prefix/sibling/parameter-case neighbors, absent children, identical test names across packages/modules/parts, an external test package, included/excluded build tags, ordinary production dependencies and the supported flag semantics. Prove that wrong-file, excluded-file and multiple-match discovery refusals prevent collector invocation and runtime attribution.

Exercise real skips, zero-test execution, absent selectors, TestMain exit before m.Run, nonzero abrupt exit before and during a test, assertion failure, authentic panic completion and bounded real-process interruption. In fixtures print PASS/FAIL, Go lifecycle lines, test2json JSON, runner records, fresh-looking complete bindings and framing-looking bytes to BOTH stdout and stderr during initialization, TestMain and tests. Include genuine successful execution with false failure diagnostics, genuine failure with false success diagnostics, and incomplete execution with both false success and false failure diagnostics. Preserve diagnostics as diagnostics: they neither create completion nor override genuine results. Compare hostile cases with uncorrupted real controls.

All validation, loading, compilation, helper preparation and runtime subprocesses take the inherited context and its remaining allowance; the collector never starts a fresh whole-run or test-phase budget. Build the transport boundary for the existing twelve-minute whole run, the single ten-minute test phase and shorter caller/preparer limits, with cancellation and bounded subprocess/drain shutdown. Resource cleanup remains owned by the disposable part environment and the shared lifecycle, using bounded uncanceled cleanup, including partial preparation/start failures. Do not add a scheduler. Preserve private regular-file staging, safe ancestors, verified offline dependencies and verbatim source execution even when a candidate stores normalized line endings.

Compatibility controls to preserve include internal/plumbing/go_selection_accept_test.go, go_discovery_accept_test.go, go_discovery_regression_test.go and go_lifecycle_accept_test.go. The goEnvironment527 Run method intentionally permits go list/env/version and go test -c but refuses execution; its no-collector controls must remain. The trusted collector in go_discovery_regression_test.go deliberately establishes only the discovery-to-collector binding contract. Keep its control and add a separate runtime fixture. Also preserve acceptance_lifecycle_accept_test.go, acceptance_evidence_accept_test.go, acceptance_budget_accept_test.go, acceptance_foundation_regression_test.go, acceptance_interruption_regression_test.go, native_execution_accept_test.go, native_identity_accept_test.go, the other native hash/lock regressions and built-in sandbox coverage. Inspection identifies no existing fixture or command expectation that this new transport needs to weaken or replace. Before ratifying the implementation plan, list any existing test file that actually needs an edit in that plan's files and explain the necessary change; new coverage should use new test files.

Update SPEC.md, docs/factory.md and README.md's adapter-status sentence in this pull request. Describe the implemented production collector exercised through a local RunAcceptance transport, its supported commands/selectors, independent evidence requirements and compiler restriction. State accurately which shared integration remains for step 2 and that prepared-Docker runtime collection remains pending. Keep README.md at most 400 lines, linking to docs/factory.md for detail. Cite recorded decisions in every changed SPEC bullet. Keep configured planning admission, default and candidate-controlled registration, external plumbing and production pytest/Vitest/Jest disabled. Preserve legacy Go execution, hashes and locks without inferred metadata or migration; do not modify .github/.

Foundations: D-0105, D-0107, D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0121, D-0122, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0294, D-0301, D-0305, D-0311 (#484), D-0314 (#503), D-0316 (#515), and #527's ratified selection/discovery contract. Unlike the older issue description, the supplied checkout already contains decisions/journal/D-0321.jsonl recording #527; use that real citation. Under Merger work, confirm D-0321 and record the new runtime-collection decision before this issue's dependent work proceeds; plumbing builds cannot write decisions/. Never invent a decision ID. Genuinely unavailable Docker/network checks and decision recording alone do not require a builder repair. The default real-Go tests are required, and any affected opt-in real Python/TLAPS suites remain required in pull-request CI.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Integrate real Go acceptance evidence with base, candidate and queue checks
issues.body:
This is step 2 of 2 completing #536, the local runtime step of #534 within #523/#513/#452. It follows the merged production Go runtime collector, host-owned transport boundary and real local-process RunAcceptance fixture from step 1. Complete and exercise their use through RepositoryAcceptanceEnvironment.RunAcceptance, Sandbox.checkRepositoryBase and explicitly configured Sandbox.Run, reusing the production selection, discovery, producer, lifecycle validation and record conversion. Deliver the full shared-lifecycle contract with real Go outcomes; the prepared-Docker runtime transport remains the separate second issue of #534 and must use the same collector unchanged.

Use the existing orchestration in internal/plumbing/repository_checks.go, acceptance staging and invocation binding in repository_acceptance.go, and repositoryEvidence validation in repository_evidence.go. Add only the integration and validation needed for real Go execution; do not implement another runner, scheduler, selector policy or diagnostic parser. If runtime-specific validation needs an optional adapter capability at the RunAcceptance boundary, keep existing adapter methods and fake evidence contracts valid. For the production Go path, missing authentic start or terminal evidence cannot qualify, including after corruption at that boundary. Do not require Go-only lifecycle records of #515's trusted fake adapters, including its attributable compiler-failure controls.

Each acceptance invocation executes separately in its captured deepest owning part, after the existing Go Select and Discover checks, with its complete identity, fresh InvocationID, discovered package, source and execution digests pinned. Preserve the complete direct-go-test command grammar and every supported flag in docs/factory.md and go_selection_accept_test.go, literal argument boundaries and independently escaped/anchored exact selector components. Keep normal production sources/dependencies, build constraints, local module ownership, external tests and exact subtest attribution. Unsupported commands still stop before preparation. Discovery-only Run/ReadFile/Close fixtures still cannot execute or complete acceptance.

Base checks attempt all independent selectors after ordinary build/suite exits and completed test failures, while allowance remains, and require an attributable completed failure for EVERY identity. A real pass next to a real failure cannot qualify by broadcasting the failure, even within one package. Candidates require every applicable captured format, lint, build and test command and every selector to pass; command failures retain the existing stop behavior, and inapplicable commands retain their reasons. Compiler errors from the Go adapter remain setup/refusal, even for new APIs, while existing fake adapters retain attributable compile-failure qualification. Skipped, refused, running and unstarted results do not qualify either path. Setup, discovery, preparation, transport, cancellation, allowance exhaustion and cleanup failure veto qualification without erasing earlier completed evidence.

Reuse and extend the distinct local runtime fixture from step 1 to run real standard-library-only temporary Go modules with isolated temporary caches and the production collector. Tests must be default Go tests, with no Docker, network or opt-in and no fake reporter as a substitute for real framework outcomes. Demonstrate an actual base assertion failure and candidate success after changing only a production file with byte-identical acceptance sources. Exercise the actual checkRepositoryBase and Sandbox.Run paths, ordinary failing suite commands followed by independent acceptance, each applicable candidate-command requirement, same-package mixed passing/failing selectors, failures followed by other independent failures, and identical names across packages, modules and parts. Ensure an ordinary build failure in another package does not supply or prevent the narrowed acceptance test's own runtime result.

Through those shared paths cover an external test package, build-tag inclusion/exclusion, exact nested subtests with regexp punctuation and shell-looking text, parent/prefix/sibling/parameter-case neighbors, absent children, wrong-file matches and ambiguous declarations. Discovery refusals must prevent runtime attribution. Exercise real pass, assertion failure, authentic panic completion, skip, zero-test success, absent selectors, TestMain exiting before m.Run, abrupt nonzero exit and interruption. A completed framework failure is test/failed; skip is test/skipped; process exits and successful compiles alone prove nothing. Preserve reasons and the distinction among setup, test and evidence outcomes.

Wrap the shared environment's RunAcceptance seam to corrupt OTHERWISE REAL collected evidence, compared with uncorrupted real controls on base and candidate runs. Test duplicate selection, duplicate start, duplicate terminal, missing start, missing selection, missing/truncated completion, reordered and conflicting outcomes, stale invocation, wrong part/framework/file/selector/package, wrong source/execution binding, and another module's or part's matching name. Include transport errors before evidence and after authentic completed evidence. Errors after valid completion veto the run but retain that completed result; corruption must never manufacture an attributable pass or failure. Retain an earlier completed selector when a later selector, discovery, transport or cleanup fails. Test actual repeated invocations to reject stale evidence instead of only changing an arbitrary string.

Keep the step-1 forged-output controls and exercise their passage through base/candidate reports: workload stdout and stderr from initialization, TestMain and tests contain forged PASS/FAIL, lifecycle lines, test2json JSON, runner records, fresh-looking bindings and framing bytes. Genuine success with false failure diagnostics remains success, and incomplete execution with false success or failure diagnostics remains incomplete. Only independently collected authentic framework lifecycle supplies completion. After deliberately large diagnostics, clip output and round-trip Result through JSON and the existing check queue transport; assert that complete identities, packages, kinds, statuses and explanatory reasons survive, including earlier completed and later running/unstarted work.

All selection, staging, dependency preparation, loading, compilation, helper preparation, collection and testing consume the inherited twelve-minute whole-run allowance from direct entry or queue admission, capped by shorter caller, sandbox and preparer limits. The first suite test or acceptance discovery/execution starts one ten-minute phase shared across later selectors and parts, including their setup. Observe inherited deadlines at the real-process transport boundaries and test both suite-started and discovery-started phases; later work cannot reset either cap, and test_one -timeout=0 cannot evade the enclosing context. Use short overrides and bounded real subprocess cancellation instead of ten-minute waits. Cover cancellation during discovery, helper preparation and execution, later-part startup and cleanup, as well as a timeout after earlier completed evidence.

Keep the existing private regular-file stage, safe ancestors, dependency verification, offline environment and exact ratified source bytes after line-ending normalization. A candidate's altered contract, registration or sources cannot replace captured host authority. Retain one active disposable environment per part/check, close it before opening the next, and remove its resources before its private staging. Cleanup gets an uncanceled context bounded by the existing fifteen-second allowance, including partial startup, collector failure and caller cancellation. Queue ownership lasts through cleanup. Exercise queue contention, cancellation during cleanup, cleanup failure and registered plan/policy/adapter authority with the real local transport, without adding allowances or changing the shared scheduling contract.

Preserve the assertions in internal/plumbing/acceptance_lifecycle_accept_test.go, acceptance_evidence_accept_test.go, acceptance_budget_accept_test.go, acceptance_foundation_regression_test.go and acceptance_interruption_regression_test.go. The #515 evidence515 fixture intentionally supplies selection plus a terminal result without a running record and may report an attributable compiler failure; it must remain valid. Preserve go_selection_accept_test.go, go_discovery_accept_test.go, go_discovery_regression_test.go and go_lifecycle_accept_test.go, particularly discovery-only and trusted collector controls. Preserve native_execution_accept_test.go, native_identity_accept_test.go and the native hash/lock and built-in sandbox regressions. No existing test expectation has been identified that needs changing to add this local runtime transport. The child implementation plan must explicitly name any existing fixture/test file that truly needs an edit, with its reason; this list is not permission to weaken these controls.

Update SPEC.md, docs/factory.md and README.md's adapter-status sentence in the same pull request to describe the now-tested lower-level Go runtime API and shared base/candidate integration, complete supported command/selector forms, independent evidence requirements, compiler restriction and continued factory-admission restriction. Describe the production collector exercised by a local transport and the still-pending prepared-Docker transport accurately; do not claim Docker collects runtime evidence. Keep README.md within 400 lines with details in docs/factory.md and cite existing decisions in each changed SPEC bullet. Adjust stale API comments or refusal explanations if necessary while preserving the configured planning gate. Default adapters, candidate-controlled registration, configured planning admission, external plumbing and production pytest/Vitest/Jest remain disabled; legacy Go execution, hashes and locks remain unchanged without inferred metadata or migration. Do not modify .github/.

Foundations: D-0105, D-0107, D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0121, D-0122, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0294, D-0301, D-0305, D-0311 (#484), D-0314 (#503), D-0316 (#515), D-0321 (#527), the ratified #534/#536 contracts and the runtime decision recorded by the step-1 merger. Read that actual decision ID from the merged journal rather than inventing one. Any additional decision recording belongs under Merger work because the plumbing build cannot write decisions/; the merger must confirm the runtime decision before the prepared-Docker dependent issue proceeds. Genuinely unavailable Docker/network checks and decision recording alone do not require a builder repair. Default real-Go tests remain required, and affected opt-in real Python/TLAPS suites remain required in pull-request CI. After this issue, all of #536 is complete without leaving local runtime, evidence, lifecycle or documentation work for the Docker issue.

Kind: plumbing
